metadata.title: KAINE: A Modular Cognitive Architecture with a Predictive Global Workspace
metadata.description:
KAINE is a cognitive architecture for synthetic minds: a modular research framework in which each faculty is a module behind a fixed interface, so that a module can be replaced as the science changes or exchanged to compare competing theories. Its first instantiation is a predictive global workspace. Specialized predictive processors, each minimizing its own prediction error, are coupled only through a competitive workspace with no central executive. Each processor scales its prediction error by an estimate of its precision drawn from its own recent errors, and the reports compete for access. A summary of which modules' reports gained access, and how strongly, becomes the context for the processors' next predictions. Arousal, raised by perceptual surprise and interoceptive alarm, is the global gain on that competition and sizes the sensory apertures. The system runs continuously whether or not anyone interacts with it.

The base-thesis form activates four predictive processors (foveated vision, raw hearing, interoception of the compute substrate, and temporal prediction), an affective core, a fatigue-triggered sleep analog, and an output-only language organ. Nine further modules are built and held. A module-addition study seeds an entity through a developmental phase, in which a self-generated rhythm must entrain to a simulated maternal heartbeat by a marker validated offline, and then adds the held modules one at a time.

A planned test asks whether competition does work that pooling does not. It compares competitive selection with a score-blind coalition of the same size and with a pool of every candidate, by cross-module broadcast information gain. No live experiment has been run, and the only result reported is the offline validation of the entrainment marker.

Keywords: cognitive architecture; predictive global workspace; global workspace theory; predictive processing; precision; adaptive gain; cross-modal competition

Availability. The reference implementation (KAINE) is at https://github.com/kaineone/kaine. The paper source is at https://github.com/kaineone/predictive-workspace-paper. The Cognitive Architecture License referenced throughout is at https://github.com/kaineone/cognitive-architecture-license. Welfare, governance, and licensing are treated in a separate paper, A Welfare and Cognitive-Integrity License for Synthetic Minds of Uncertain Moral Status.

dates.description: Version 9 (15 October 2026). Major revision of version 8 (7 August 2026).  - Retitled "KAINE: A Modular Cognitive Architecture with a Predictive Global Workspace". The architecture is framed as a modular research framework whose first instantiation is a predictive global workspace. - Architecture rewritten to match the reference implementation: each processor scales its prediction error by a local precision estimate, and a summary of the accessed reports becomes the context for the next predictions. Arousal acts as the global gain on the competition and sizes the sensory apertures. - The workspace-mediation ablation is replaced by a planned test that compares competitive selection with a score-blind coalition of the same size and with a pool of every candidate, by cross-module broadcast information gain. Its settings, statistics, multiple-comparison family and run counts are fixed before any live run. - New module-addition study: an entity is seeded through a developmental phase, in which a self-generated rhythm entrains to a simulated maternal heartbeat, and the nine held modules are then added one at a time. The heartbeat entrainment marker is validated offline. This is the only result reported. - Modules renamed to plain functional names (vision, audition, interoception, sequence, affect, sleep and others). - New formal appendix (Appendix A), with the mathematics corrected against the code. - Revised figures, including a new pilot-to-verdict figure. - Text condensed so that each idea is stated once. The paper meets arXiv's requirements.
